assumptions: Archived dry Warp runs: 100 ug/m3, 1 m/s wind, 0.01 m/s settling, capture probability 1, one hour. Scale mass linearly to 10 ug/m3 and repeat uniform hourly deposition.
Four winds have equal weights in dry deposition and rain exposure. These are not measured wind frequencies.
Use seed-mean then wind-mean fluxes and exposure; assume spatially uniform mass on each family/face. Unlike the single rain-event experiment, do not resolve individual modules.
Deposit first, then rain wash, then evaluate power at the end-of-hour dust state. Retain separate loose and bound pools across all events.

Use only the HSU mass-to-transmission relation with g/m2 units; do not use its complete-cleaning reset or gravitational cos(tilt) deposition model. Treat application to both faces and dust composition as uncalibrated.

Freeze clean-reference Faiman module temperature for both clean and dirty power, isolating optical loss. Monofacial temperature uses front irradiance only, bifacial uses front+rear, matching manuscript v0.5. Do not solve thermal feedback or electrical mismatch.
Treat common 8% DC loss as fixed non-soiling loss in this extension; add explicit optical soiling separately. Inverter efficiency 96%, DC/AC ratio 1.2.
Same 1m clear gap, assumed 0.5m minimum vertical strip, 1.1m slant length, 0.8m clearance; report AC per kWp rather than unequal site capacities.
Existing TMY midpoint interpretation is preserved; documented irradiance timing limitations remain.
Sensitivity multipliers are scenario ranges, not probabilities or confidence intervals. No ESS or cost recalculation is included.
10 repeated non-leap 365-day TMY years; no observed 10-year weather record or climate forecast. Dust persists across year boundaries.
No manual cleaning and no equipment aging. Optical dust loss is isolated; annual degradation is fixed at zero.
Rain every 14 days across all 3650 days, at the beginning of each designated rain day. No year-boundary reset of rain phase; 260 events in 10 years.
Report 1-, 5- and 10-year checkpoints. The existing first-year result is retained as a regression reference.
Daily and monthly electricity totals are NA if any hour in the interval is outside the adopted optical mass range. Mass estimates continue but remain scenario-dependent.
No weeds and no snow, as specified by the user; no vegetation shading, snow cover, snowmelt cleaning or snow albedo adjustment.
out_of_domain: Do not evaluate HSU above 10 g/m2 on any electricity-producing face. Report NA rather than clip or extrapolate. Cumulative energy is NA if any included hour is invalid.

site_conditions.note: User-specified boundary conditions: no weeds or snow. Existing calculations already omitted these effects.
